            # stops the job right here - so the published session kept saying
            # "live" and the panel handed out a tunnel that is already dead.
            # Close the slot from the trap instead, after the writers above
            # are gone so the ended marker cannot race them.
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=hub-linux" "state=ended" \
              >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            exit "$code"
          }
          trap 'cleanup_watchdog 143' TERM INT
          # Watch the hub and the tunnel instead of sleeping blindly: a dead
          # hub behind a live tunnel answers 502, and a dead tunnel keeps
          # resolving - both look like "the address is there but nothing
          # opens". Either one is restarted here; a new tunnel address is
          # republished so the panel never points at a corpse.
          HUBDIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/npm-hub"
          # open_tunnel.sh writes the pid under $HUB_LOGS (~/.npm-hub/logs/);
          # reading those paths is what lets the watchdog verify the tunnel
          # instead of re-opening it every loop (the /tmp path never existed
          # -> the tunnel was declared dead every ~90s and reconnected
          # endlessly).
          RESTARTING=0
          FAILS=0
          HUB_PID="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          for i in $(seq 1 1400); do
            sleep 15
            # The session relay wrote this marker right before it exited: the
            # work is saved and the next runner has published itself. Restarting
            # the hub now would resurrect the runner we just handed over, so the
            # watchdog ends the job cleanly instead.
            if [ -f "$HUB_LOGS/handoff-done" ]; then
              echo "handoff complete - the session lives on the next runner now."
              cleanup_watchdog 0
            fi
            # One missed probe is NOT a dead hub: the box saturates its CPU
            # launching a game / a build and a 10s curl can legitimately bleed
            # over. Only restart after several consecutive misses, so a single
            # spike doesn't kill the hub and drop every attached tab.
            if hub_ready; then
              FAILS=0
            else
              FAILS=$((FAILS + 1))
              echo "::warning::hub probe missed ($FAILS consecutive)."
            fi
            if [ "$FAILS" -ge 3 ] && [ "$RESTARTING" = "0" ]; then
              echo "::warning::hub stopped answering ($FAILS misses); restarting it."
              RESTARTING=1
              # Brackets, not a plain string: pkill -f matches its own
              # parent shell's command line too, and a plain pattern is
              # suicide - measured the hard way.
              if [ -n "${HUB_PID:-}" ]; then kill "$HUB_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
              cd "$HUBDIR"
              SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)"
              HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="$HUB_TOKEN_VALUE" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' GH_TOKEN='${{ inputs.gh_token }}' PORT="$HUB_PORT" SESSION_STARTED_MS="$SESSION_STARTED_MS" SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
              HUB_PID=$!
              echo "$HUB_PID" > "$HUB_PID_FILE"
              # Wait for the new hub to serve again before probing it for
              # "dead": otherwise the first check hits it mid-boot and the
              # watchdog loops on itself forever.
              for boot in $(seq 1 12); do
                if hub_ready; then
                  FAILS=0; RESTARTING=0
                  echo "::warning::hub is back."
                  break
                fi
                sleep 5
              done
              # Boot wait exhausted: release the restart lock so a hub that
              # really died at boot is tried again (otherwise the watchdog
              # locks itself out and never recovers).
              if [ "$RESTARTING" = "1" ]; then
                echo "::warning::hub did not come back; a later restart will retry."
                RESTARTING=0; FAILS=0
              fi
            fi
            CUR=$(cat $HUB_LOGS/hub-url 2>/dev/null || echo)
            PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo)
            EDGE=""
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$CUR" ] \
              && bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_health.sh" "$CUR" "/"; then
              EDGE=1
            fi
            if [ -n "$EDGE" ]; then continue; fi
            # Drop the stale cloudflared before a fresh one takes the port:
            # stacking instances leaks processes and burns tunnel names.
            # Bracket pattern - a plain "cloudflared tunnel..." match is
            # suicide against this shell's own command line.
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
            pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090" 2>/dev/null || true
            sleep 1
            echo "::warning::tunnel dead; reopening."
            URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 8090 $HUB_LOGS/tunnel2.log) || continue
            [ -n "$URL" ] || continue
            echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/hub-url
            echo "back up on $URL"
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
                "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
                "url=$URL" "hubUrl=$URL" "desktop=$URL/d" "mobile=$URL/m" \
                $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2")") \
                "auth=без пароля" "label=${{ inputs.label }}"
          done
          cleanup_watchdog 0

      - name: Final durable repository and session backup
        if: always()
        timeout-minutes: 6
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" --once \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log"

      - name: Clear the published session
        if: always()
        run: |
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=hub-linux" "state=ended"

      - name: Snapshot audit/code on exit
        if: always()
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          # --once always exports this repo's chats; SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1
          # additionally exports chats/<name>.json for every repo under $HOME.
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" --once hub "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" 2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-hub.log"

      - name: Save the models snapshot
        if: always()
        run: |
          # Whatever the live registry learned before shutdown, in one small
          # object the panel renders as a line. The hub may already be dead
          # here (cancelled mid-run) - then the file stays empty and json=
          # is skipped with a warning.
          mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          python3 - > $HUB_LOGS/hub-models.json <<'PY' || true
          import json, urllib.request
          _zt = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/models/full', headers={'x-hub-token': '${{ inputs.token }}'})
          d = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(_zt, timeout=20))
          ms = d.get('models', [])
          free = [m for m in ms if m.get('free')]
          print(json.dumps({
              'kind': 'NPM-Hub',
              'hubCount': len(ms),
              'hubFree': len(free),
              'hubTop': [(m.get('fullId') or m.get('id')) for m in free[:8]],
              'hubSelected': d.get('selected') or '',
          }))
          PY
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
              "slot=hub-linux" "file=models-hub-linux.json" \
               "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
              "json=$HUB_LOGS/hub-models.json"

      - name: Record the run in the history
        if: always()
        run: |
          # One small file per run, filed under the day and the weekday it
          # belongs to: history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - the
          # diary the panel groups by day, and unlike the Actions UI it does not
          # disappear when GitHub prunes old runs.
          STARTED=""
          if [ -f "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" ]; then
            STARTED="$(date -u -d "@$(( $(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) / 1000 ))" '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 \
              "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
              "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" \
              ${STARTED:+journal_date="$STARTED"} \
              "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" \
              "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" \
              2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "::warning::run history record failed"

  # ── Hub on Windows ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  hub-windows:
    if: inputs.os == 'windows'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_windows }}
    timeout-minutes: 360

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      # The gate token is echoed into this job's logs by the shell (every
      # x-hub-token probe line). Mask it before anything prints it.
      - name: Mask the gate token in logs
        if: inputs.token != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          ZT_MASK: ${{ inputs.token }}
          GH_MASK: ${{ inputs.gh_token }}
        run: |
          echo "::add-mask::$ZT_MASK"
          echo "::add-mask::$GH_MASK"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Restore the npm/pip caches
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.npm
            ~/AppData/Local/pip/Cache
          key: hub-pkg-windows-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: hub-pkg-windows-

      - name: Install the CLI agents
        if: inputs.preinstall
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # One npm call first (concurrent downloads, minutes faster), then
          # single retries only for commands still missing - a renamed
          # package cannot cancel the rest. Anything missing still launches
          # through `npx -y` at click time.
          $want = @(
            @('opencode-ai', 'opencode'), @('@anthropic-ai/claude-code', 'claude'),
            @('@google/gemini-cli', 'gemini'), @('@openai/codex', 'codex'),
            @('@github/copilot', 'copilot'), @('@qwen-code/qwen-code', 'qwen'),
            @('http-server', 'http-server')
          )
          npm install -g ($want | ForEach-Object { $_[0] }) 2>&1 | Out-Null
          foreach ($pair in $want) {
            if (-not (Get-Command $pair[1] -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
              npm install -g $pair[0] 2>&1 | Out-Null
            }
          }
          pip install aider-chat goose-ai 2>&1 | Out-Null
          foreach ($c in @('opencode', 'claude', 'gemini', 'codex', 'copilot', 'qwen', 'aider', 'goose', 'http-server')) {
            $hit = Get-Command $c -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Write-Host ("  {0}: {1}" -f $c, ($(if ($hit) { $hit.Source } else { '-' })))
          }

      - name: Install the hub dependencies
        working-directory: fork/npm-hub
        run: npm ci

      - name: Put zen-agent on PATH
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bindir = "$env:USERPROFILE/bin"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $bindir | Out-Null
          @('@echo off', ('node "' + $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE + '/fork/agent/zen-agent.js" %*')) | Set-Content "$bindir/agent.cmd"
          Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH $bindir

      - name: Install OpenCode for session recovery
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bin = "$env:USERPROFILE\.opencode\bin"
          Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH $bin
          Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin"
          $env:Path = "$bin;$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin;$env:Path"
          if (-not (Get-Command opencode -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
            npm install -g opencode-ai
          }
          if (-not (Get-Command opencode -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
            throw "OpenCode installation failed; previous sessions cannot be restored"
          }
          opencode --version

      - name: Create the work folder
        run: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\hub-work" | Out-Null

      - name: Restore repositories and OpenCode sessions
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$HOME/hub-work" "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"
          WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE_EXISTING=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore-work.sh"
          bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork"
          RESTORE_CHATS_ALL=1 RESTORE_CHATS_ROOT="$HOME" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$HOME/hub-work"

      - name: Start the hub and open the tunnel
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          Set-Location "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\npm-hub"

          # cmd /c start, NOT Start-Process: a process started with
          # Start-Process is killed when its step ends (measured on a live
          # runner with the agent). Redirects are not optional either:
          # without them pwsh waits on the child's stdout forever.
          $env:PORT = '8090'
          $env:HUB_PORT_STRICT = '1'
          $env:HUB_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.token }}'; $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.gh_token }}'
          $SESSION_FILE = "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\session-start.txt"
          [System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $SESSION_FILE))
          [IO.File]::WriteAllText($SESSION_FILE, [string][int64]([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()))
          $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = ([IO.File]::ReadAllText($SESSION_FILE)).Trim()
          $env:SESSION_LIMIT_MS = "21600000"
          cmd /c start "" /b node src/server.js `
            "1>$env:TEMP\hub.log" "2>$env:TEMP\hub.err"

          $up = $false
          foreach ($i in 1..60) {
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
            try {
              $r = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 15 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}
              if ($r.success -and -not $r.warming -and $r.runId -eq '${{ github.run_id }}') { $up = $true; break }
            } catch { }
          }
          if (-not $up) {
            Write-Host '::error::the hub did not start.'
            Get-Content "$env:TEMP\hub.log", "$env:TEMP\hub.err" -Tail 40 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            exit 1
          }
          Write-Host 'hub is up on 8090'

          # curl.exe, not Invoke-WebRequest: the .NET stack fails GitHub's
          # redirect with RemoteCertificateNameMismatch (measured before).
          $cf = "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe"
          curl.exe -sL --retry 3 -o $cf `
            'https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-windows-amd64.exe'
          if (-not (Test-Path $cf)) { throw 'could not download cloudflared' }

          $log = "$env:TEMP\cf.log"
          cmd /c start "" /b "$cf" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
            "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf.err"

          $url = $null
          foreach ($i in 1..40) {
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
            $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
            if ($text -match 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com') { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
          }
          if (-not $url) {
            Write-Host '::error::no tunnel came up.'
            Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            exit 1
          }

          $edgeReady = $false
          $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-tunnel-probe.html"
          foreach ($i in 1..30) {
            $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 15 "$url/"
            $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeReady = $true; break }
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
          }
          if (-not $edgeReady) {
            Write-Host '::error::Cloudflare edge did not become ready (Error 1033).'
            Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            exit 1
          }
          $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline

          try {
            $tools = (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 10 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}).tools `
              | Where-Object { $_.installed } | ForEach-Object { $_.name }
            $toolsLine = $tools -join ', '
          } catch { $toolsLine = 'n/a' }
          if (-not $toolsLine) { $toolsLine = 'none detected' }

          $summary = @(
            '## NPM Hub (Windows)',
            '',
            "**[Open the hub]($url)** - no password, pick Desktop or Mobile.",
            '',
            '| | |',
            '|---|---|',
            "| Address | ``$url`` |",
            "| Desktop | ``$url/d`` |",
            "| Mobile | ``$url/m`` |",
            "| CLI agents | $toolsLine |",
            '| Runner | windows-latest, 4 cores, 16 GB |'
          ) -join "`n"
          $summary | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY -Append
          Write-Host '=================================================='
          Write-Host " Hub: $url"
          Write-Host " Tools: $toolsLine"
          Write-Host '=================================================='

          $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
            'slot=hub-windows' 'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
            "url=$url" "hubUrl=$url" "desktop=$url/d" "mobile=$url/m" `
            'auth=без пароля' "tools=$toolsLine" `
            'label=${{ inputs.label }}'

      - name: Keep the session alive
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # Same watchdog as the Linux job: restart a dead hub, reopen a
          # dead tunnel, republish a changed address - so the panel never
          # points at a corpse.
          $hubDir = "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\npm-hub"
          $cf = "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe"
          # One missed probe is NOT a dead hub (a game build saturates the
          # CPU), and `Stop-Process -Name node` would kill the user's own
          # node-based app together with the hub. Only restart after several
          # consecutive misses, and kill ONLY the hub's own process.
          $hubUp = $false
          $fails = 0
          $restartingHub = $false
          for ($i = 1; $i -le 700; $i++) {
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 30
            # The session relay wrote this marker right before it exited: the
            # work is saved and the next runner has published itself. Bringing
            # the hub back would resurrect the runner we just handed over, so
            # tear this one down and let the job finish.
            if (Test-Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\logs\handoff-done") {
              Write-Host 'handoff complete - the session lives on the next runner now.'
              Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*src/server.js*' } |
                ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
              Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
              break
            }
            $hubUp = $false
            try {
              Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 20 -UseBasicParsing -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'} | Out-Null
              $hubUp = $true
            } catch { }
            if ($hubUp) {
              $fails = 0; $restartingHub = $false; $hubUp = $false
            } else {
              $fails++
              Write-Host "::warning::hub probe missed ($fails consecutive)."
            }
            if ($fails -ge 3 -and -not $restartingHub) {
              Write-Host '::warning::hub stopped answering; restarting it.'
              $restartingHub = $true
              # Kill only this hub (src/server.js), leaving the user's own
              # node processes (an app, a game launcher) untouched.
              Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*src/server.js*' } |
                ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
              Set-Location $hubDir
              $env:PORT = '8090'
              $env:HUB_PORT_STRICT = '1'
              $env:HUB_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.token }}'; $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.gh_token }}'
              $env:HUB_LABEL = '${{ inputs.label }}'
              $SESSION_FILE = "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\session-start.txt"
              $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = ((Get-Content $SESSION_FILE -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Trim())
              if (-not $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS) { $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = [string][int64]([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()) }
              $env:SESSION_LIMIT_MS = "21600000"
              cmd /c start "" /b node src/server.js "1>>$env:TEMP\hub.log" "2>>$env:TEMP\hub.err"
              # Wait for the new hub to serve before probing it again, so the
              # freshly booting process isn't counted as a missed probe.
              foreach ($boot in 1..12) {
                Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
                try {
                  Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 20 -UseBasicParsing -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'} | Out-Null
                  $fails = 0; $restartingHub = $false
                  Write-Host '::warning::hub is back.'
                  break
                } catch { }
              }
              # Boot wait exhausted: release the restart lock so a hub that
              # really died at boot is tried again.
              if ($restartingHub) {
                Write-Host '::warning::hub did not come back; a later restart will retry.'
                $restartingHub = $false; $fails = 0
              }
            }
            $cur = ''
            try { $cur = (Get-Content "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Raw -ErrorAction Stop).Trim() } catch { }
            $edgeOk = $false
            if ((Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and $cur) {
              try {
                $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-watch-probe.html"
                $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 10 "$cur/"
                $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
                if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeOk = $true }
              } catch { }
            }
            if ($edgeOk) { continue }
            Write-Host '::warning::tunnel dead; reopening.'
            Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            $log = "$env:TEMP\cf2.log"
            cmd /c start "" /b "$cf" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
              "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf2.err"
            $url = $null
            foreach ($k in 1..40) {
              Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
              $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf2.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
              if ($text -match 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com') { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
            }
            if (-not $url) { continue }
            $edgeReady = $false
            $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-tunnel-probe2.html"
            foreach ($k in 1..30) {
              $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 15 "$url/"
              $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
              if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeReady = $true; break }
              Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
            }
            if (-not $edgeReady) { continue }
            $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
            Write-Host "back up on $url"
            $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
            bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
              'slot=hub-windows' 'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
              "url=$url" "hubUrl=$url" "desktop=$url/d" "mobile=$url/m" `
              'auth=без пароля' 'label=${{ inputs.label }}'
          }

      - name: Final durable repository backup
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" --once \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log"

      - name: Snapshot audit/code on exit
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" --once hub "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-hub.log"

      - name: Clear the published session
        if: always()
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" 'slot=hub-windows' 'state=ended'

      - name: Save the models snapshot
        if: always()
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          try {
            $d = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/models/full' -TimeoutSec 20 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}
            $ms = @($d.models)
            $free = @($ms | Where-Object { $_.free })
            $obj = [ordered]@{
              kind = 'NPM-Hub'
              hubCount = $ms.Count
              hubFree = $free.Count
              hubTop = @($free | Select-Object -First 8 | ForEach-Object { $_.fullId })
              hubSelected = $d.selected
            }
            ($obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4) | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-models.json" -Encoding utf8
          } catch { }
          $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
            'slot=hub-windows' 'file=models-hub-windows.json' `
            'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
            "json=$env:TEMP\hub-models.json"

      - name: Export OpenCode chats for all repositories
        # Runs even on a cancelled/expired job so the NEXT windows run can
        # restore every repo's sessions (chats/<name>.json -> session-state).
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CHAT_ALL_ROOT="$HOME" PUBLISH=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/export-chats.sh" --all \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/export-chats.log"

      - name: Record the run in the history
        if: always()
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - see the Linux step.
          $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 `
            "slot=hub-windows" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=windows" `
            "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$([DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ'))" `
            "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" `
            "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"

  # ── Linux Desktop VNC (parallel runner) ────────────────────────────────
  # A second, independent job next to `hub`. It stands up a headless Linux
  # desktop (openbox + xterm, Mesa software rendering) and exposes it through
  # x11vnc + noVNC + a cloudflared tunnel from the very start of the run, so
  # the hub gets a working graphical shell (an "Open the Linux screen" button)
  # without ever pressing Start. Kept alive by the same watchdog pattern as
  # the hub: dead desktop/tunnel gets restarted in-place.
  vnc:
    if: inputs.os == 'linux'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
    timeout-minutes: 360

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      - name: Install the desktop + VNC stack
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq \
            xvfb openbox xterm tint2 idesk x11vnc websockify novnc dbus-x11 \
            mesa-utils libgl1-mesa-dri libgl1 libegl1 libgles2 \
            libglu1-mesa libgbm1 x11-utils x11-xserver-utils \
            pcmanfm pulseaudio pavucontrol

      - name: Start the Linux desktop and open the tunnel
        run: |
          export VNC_PORT=5901 NOVNC_PORT=6081
          bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/start_desktop.sh" || {
            echo "::error::the Linux desktop VNC did not start."
            tail -30 $HUB_LOGS/xvfb.log $HUB_LOGS/openbox.log $HUB_LOGS/x11vnc.log 2>/dev/null
            exit 1
          }

          URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 6081 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel.log)
          if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
            echo "::error::no tunnel for the VNC desktop."
            tail -25 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/vnc-url

          # Pre-warm: the noVNC page must answer over the tunnel edge before
          # we hand the address to the panel.
          for i in $(seq 1 20); do
            code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 10 "$URL/vnc.html" || true)
            case "$code" in 2*|3*|4*) break ;; esac
            sleep 3
          done

          {
            echo "## Linux Desktop (VNC)"
            echo ""
            echo "**[Open the Linux screen]($URL/vnc.html)** - openbox + xterm + Mesa."
            echo ""
            echo "| | |"
            echo "|---|---|"
            echo "| noVNC | \`$URL/vnc.html\` |"
            echo "| VNC | \`127.0.0.1:5901\` (on the runner) |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          echo "=================================================="
          echo " Linux Desktop VNC: $URL/vnc.html"
          echo "=================================================="

          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
              "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
              "url=$URL/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$URL/vnc.html" \
              $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2")") \
              "label=${{ inputs.label }}"

          # Z11 dual tunnel on the desktop VM as well.
          nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_keeper.sh" vnc >> "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.pid"
          echo "tunnel keeper: vnc endpoint now carries main + reserve addresses"

          # Same lifelines as the hub job (Z10): this VM holds the desktop the
          # user actually watches - when the hub VM wedges, the queue + tmate
          # here stay reachable. Beacons land in control/rescue-vnc.json and
          # control/heartbeat-vnc.json, commands pick target=vnc.
          if [ "${{ inputs.rescue_ssh }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=vnc \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/rescue_ssh.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.pid"
            echo "rescue ssh daemon (vnc vm): -> control/rescue-vnc.json"
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.command_queue }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=vnc \
              HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/hub_control.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.pid"
            echo "control daemon (vnc vm): queue + heartbeat; reopen-tunnel reopens the VNC tunnel"
          fi

      - name: Keep the VNC session alive
        run: |
          PIDFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-6081.pid"
          cleanup_vnc() {
            local code="${1:-143}"
            trap - TERM INT
            if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
              local pid; pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
              [ -z "$pid" ] || kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            pkill -f "websockify.*6081" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:6081" 2>/dev/null || true
            # Background lifelines started above: same "Complete job" hang rule.
            pkill -f "[h]ub_control.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[r]escue_ssh.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[t]unnel_keeper.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            rm -f "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-6081-reserve.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            tmate -S "$HUB_LOGS/tmate.sock" kill-session >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            # The X stack is started detached by start_desktop.sh and the
            # runner waits for it too - leaving Xvfb/openbox/x11vnc running
            # hangs "Complete job" exactly like the hub's daemons did.
            pkill -f "Xvfb ${VNC_DISPLAY:-:99}" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[o]penbox" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "x11vnc.*${VNC_DISPLAY:-:99}" 2>/dev/null || true
            # Same as the hub job: `if: always()` does not survive a cancel.
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=vnc" "state=ended" \
              >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            exit "$code"
          }
          trap 'cleanup_vnc 143' TERM INT
          VFAILS=0
          VRESTARTING=0
          for i in $(seq 1 1400); do
            sleep 15
            # Same rule as the hub watchdog: a busy CPU (a game or a build in
            # the desktop) can make one probe bleed over its timeout. Restart
            # the desktop only after several consecutive misses, and only if a
            # restart is not already in progress.
            if curl -sf -o /dev/null -m 20 "http://127.0.0.1:6081/vnc.html"; then
              VFAILS=0
            else
              VFAILS=$((VFAILS + 1))
              echo "::warning::VNC probe missed ($VFAILS consecutive)."
            fi
            if [ "$VFAILS" -ge 3 ] && [ "$VRESTARTING" = "0" ]; then
              echo "::warning::desktop VNC stopped answering; restarting it."
              VRESTARTING=1
              pkill -f "websockify.*6081" 2>/dev/null || true
              export VNC_PORT=5901 NOVNC_PORT=6081
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/start_desktop.sh" || true
              for boot in $(seq 1 12); do
                if curl -sf -o /dev/null -m 20 "http://127.0.0.1:6081/vnc.html"; then
                  VFAILS=0; VRESTARTING=0
                  echo "::warning::VNC is back."
                  break
                fi
                sleep 5
              done
              if [ "$VRESTARTING" = "1" ]; then
                echo "::warning::VNC did not come back; a later restart will retry."
                VRESTARTING=0; VFAILS=0
              fi
            fi
            CUR=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url" 2>/dev/null || echo)
            PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo)
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$CUR" ] \
              && bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_health.sh" "$CUR" "/vnc.html"; then
              continue
            fi
            # Same stale-cloudflared cleanup as the hub job above; bracket
            # pattern so pkill never matches this shell's own command line.
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
            pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:6081" 2>/dev/null || true
            sleep 1
            echo "::warning::VNC tunnel dead; reopening."
            URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 6081 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel2.log) || continue
            [ -n "$URL" ] || continue
            echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/vnc-url
            echo "VNC back up on $URL/vnc.html"
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
                "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
                "url=$URL/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$URL/vnc.html" \
                $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2")") \
                "label=${{ inputs.label }}"
          done
          cleanup_vnc 0

      - name: Clear the published VNC session
        if: always()
        run: |
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=vnc" "state=ended"

      - name: Record the run in the history
        if: always()
        run: |
          # One small file per run, filed under the day and the weekday it
          # belongs to: history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - the
          # diary the panel groups by day, and unlike the Actions UI it does not
          # disappear when GitHub prunes old runs.
          STARTED=""
          if [ -f "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" ]; then
            STARTED="$(date -u -d "@$(( $(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) / 1000 ))" '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 \
              "slot=vnc" "kind=VNC" "os=linux" \
              "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" \
              ${STARTED:+journal_date="$STARTED"} \
              "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" \
              "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" \
              2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "::warning::run history record failed"

metadata.output:
...

s by the shell (every
      # x-hub-token probe line). Mask it before anything prints it.
      - name: Mask the gate token in logs
        if: inputs.token != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          ZT_MASK: ${{ inputs.token }}
          GH_MASK: ${{ inputs.gh_token }}
        run: |
          echo "::add-mask::$ZT_MASK"
          echo "::add-mask::$GH_MASK"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Restore the npm/pip caches
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.npm
            ~/AppData/Local/pip/Cache
          key: hub-pkg-windows-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: hub-pkg-windows-

      - name: Install the CLI agents
        if: inputs.preinstall
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # One npm call first (concurrent downloads, minutes faster), then
          # single retries only for commands still missing - a renamed
          # package cannot cancel the rest. Anything missing still launches
          # through `npx -y` at click time.
          $want = @(
            @('opencode-ai', 'opencode'), @('@anthropic-ai/claude-code', 'claude'),
            @('@google/gemini-cli', 'gemini'), @('@openai/codex', 'codex'),
            @('@github/copilot', 'copilot'), @('@qwen-code/qwen-code', 'qwen'),
            @('http-server', 'http-server')
          )
          npm install -g ($want | ForEach-Object { $_[0] }) 2>&1 | Out-Null
          foreach ($pair in $want) {
            if (-not (Get-Command $pair[1] -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
              npm install -g $pair[0] 2>&1 | Out-Null
            }
          }
          pip install aider-chat goose-ai 2>&1 | Out-Null
          foreach ($c in @('opencode', 'claude', 'gemini', 'codex', 'copilot', 'qwen', 'aider', 'goose', 'http-server')) {
            $hit = Get-Command $c -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Write-Host ("  {0}: {1}" -f $c, ($(if ($hit) { $hit.Source } else { '-' })))
          }

      - name: Install the hub dependencies
        working-directory: fork/npm-hub
        run: npm ci

      - name: Put zen-agent on PATH
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bindir = "$env:USERPROFILE/bin"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $bindir | Out-Null
          @('@echo off', ('node "' + $env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE + '/fork/agent/zen-agent.js" %*')) | Set-Content "$bindir/agent.cmd"
          Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH $bindir

      - name: Install OpenCode for session recovery
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $bin = "$env:USERPROFILE\.opencode\bin"
          Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH $bin
          Add-Content $env:GITHUB_PATH "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin"
          $env:Path = "$bin;$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin;$env:Path"
          if (-not (Get-Command opencode -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
            npm install -g opencode-ai
          }
          if (-not (Get-Command opencode -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
            throw "OpenCode installation failed; previous sessions cannot be restored"
          }
          opencode --version

      - name: Create the work folder
        run: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\hub-work" | Out-Null

      - name: Restore repositories and OpenCode sessions
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$HOME/hub-work" "$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"
          WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" WORK_BACKUP_RESTORE_EXISTING=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore-work.sh"
          bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork"
          RESTORE_CHATS_ALL=1 RESTORE_CHATS_ROOT="$HOME" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/restore_audit_code.sh" "$HOME/hub-work"

      - name: Start the hub and open the tunnel
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          Set-Location "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\npm-hub"

          # cmd /c start, NOT Start-Process: a process started with
          # Start-Process is killed when its step ends (measured on a live
          # runner with the agent). Redirects are not optional either:
          # without them pwsh waits on the child's stdout forever.
          $env:PORT = '8090'
          $env:HUB_PORT_STRICT = '1'
          $env:HUB_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.token }}'; $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.gh_token }}'
          $SESSION_FILE = "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\session-start.txt"
          [System.IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $SESSION_FILE))
          [IO.File]::WriteAllText($SESSION_FILE, [string][int64]([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()))
          $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = ([IO.File]::ReadAllText($SESSION_FILE)).Trim()
          $env:SESSION_LIMIT_MS = "21600000"
          cmd /c start "" /b node src/server.js `
            "1>$env:TEMP\hub.log" "2>$env:TEMP\hub.err"

          $up = $false
          foreach ($i in 1..60) {
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
            try {
              $r = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 15 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}
              if ($r.success -and -not $r.warming -and $r.runId -eq '${{ github.run_id }}') { $up = $true; break }
            } catch { }
          }
          if (-not $up) {
            Write-Host '::error::the hub did not start.'
            Get-Content "$env:TEMP\hub.log", "$env:TEMP\hub.err" -Tail 40 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            exit 1
          }
          Write-Host 'hub is up on 8090'

          # curl.exe, not Invoke-WebRequest: the .NET stack fails GitHub's
          # redirect with RemoteCertificateNameMismatch (measured before).
          $cf = "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe"
          curl.exe -sL --retry 3 -o $cf `
            'https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared/releases/latest/download/cloudflared-windows-amd64.exe'
          if (-not (Test-Path $cf)) { throw 'could not download cloudflared' }

          $log = "$env:TEMP\cf.log"
          cmd /c start "" /b "$cf" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
            "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf.err"

          $url = $null
          foreach ($i in 1..40) {
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
            $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
            if ($text -match 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com') { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
          }
          if (-not $url) {
            Write-Host '::error::no tunnel came up.'
            Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            exit 1
          }

          $edgeReady = $false
          $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-tunnel-probe.html"
          foreach ($i in 1..30) {
            $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 15 "$url/"
            $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeReady = $true; break }
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
          }
          if (-not $edgeReady) {
            Write-Host '::error::Cloudflare edge did not become ready (Error 1033).'
            Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf.err" -Tail 25 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            exit 1
          }
          $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline

          try {
            $tools = (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 10 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}).tools `
              | Where-Object { $_.installed } | ForEach-Object { $_.name }
            $toolsLine = $tools -join ', '
          } catch { $toolsLine = 'n/a' }
          if (-not $toolsLine) { $toolsLine = 'none detected' }

          $summary = @(
            '## NPM Hub (Windows)',
            '',
            "**[Open the hub]($url)** - no password, pick Desktop or Mobile.",
            '',
            '| | |',
            '|---|---|',
            "| Address | ``$url`` |",
            "| Desktop | ``$url/d`` |",
            "| Mobile | ``$url/m`` |",
            "| CLI agents | $toolsLine |",
            '| Runner | windows-latest, 4 cores, 16 GB |'
          ) -join "`n"
          $summary | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY -Append
          Write-Host '=================================================='
          Write-Host " Hub: $url"
          Write-Host " Tools: $toolsLine"
          Write-Host '=================================================='

          $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
            'slot=hub-windows' 'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
            "url=$url" "hubUrl=$url" "desktop=$url/d" "mobile=$url/m" `
            'auth=без пароля' "tools=$toolsLine" `
            'label=${{ inputs.label }}'

      - name: Keep the session alive
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # Same watchdog as the Linux job: restart a dead hub, reopen a
          # dead tunnel, republish a changed address - so the panel never
          # points at a corpse.
          $hubDir = "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE\fork\npm-hub"
          $cf = "$env:TEMP\cloudflared.exe"
          # One missed probe is NOT a dead hub (a game build saturates the
          # CPU), and `Stop-Process -Name node` would kill the user's own
          # node-based app together with the hub. Only restart after several
          # consecutive misses, and kill ONLY the hub's own process.
          $hubUp = $false
          $fails = 0
          $restartingHub = $false
          for ($i = 1; $i -le 700; $i++) {
            Start-Sleep -Seconds 30
            # The session relay wrote this marker right before it exited: the
            # work is saved and the next runner has published itself. Bringing
            # the hub back would resurrect the runner we just handed over, so
            # tear this one down and let the job finish.
            if (Test-Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\logs\handoff-done") {
              Write-Host 'handoff complete - the session lives on the next runner now.'
              Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*src/server.js*' } |
                ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
              Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
              break
            }
            $hubUp = $false
            try {
              Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 20 -UseBasicParsing -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'} | Out-Null
              $hubUp = $true
            } catch { }
            if ($hubUp) {
              $fails = 0; $restartingHub = $false; $hubUp = $false
            } else {
              $fails++
              Write-Host "::warning::hub probe missed ($fails consecutive)."
            }
            if ($fails -ge 3 -and -not $restartingHub) {
              Write-Host '::warning::hub stopped answering; restarting it.'
              $restartingHub = $true
              # Kill only this hub (src/server.js), leaving the user's own
              # node processes (an app, a game launcher) untouched.
              Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
                Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like '*src/server.js*' } |
                ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
              Set-Location $hubDir
              $env:PORT = '8090'
              $env:HUB_PORT_STRICT = '1'
              $env:HUB_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.token }}'; $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ inputs.gh_token }}'
              $env:HUB_LABEL = '${{ inputs.label }}'
              $SESSION_FILE = "$env:USERPROFILE\.npm-hub\session-start.txt"
              $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = ((Get-Content $SESSION_FILE -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Trim())
              if (-not $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS) { $env:SESSION_STARTED_MS = [string][int64]([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()) }
              $env:SESSION_LIMIT_MS = "21600000"
              cmd /c start "" /b node src/server.js "1>>$env:TEMP\hub.log" "2>>$env:TEMP\hub.err"
              # Wait for the new hub to serve before probing it again, so the
              # freshly booting process isn't counted as a missed probe.
              foreach ($boot in 1..12) {
                Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
                try {
                  Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/tools' -TimeoutSec 20 -UseBasicParsing -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'} | Out-Null
                  $fails = 0; $restartingHub = $false
                  Write-Host '::warning::hub is back.'
                  break
                } catch { }
              }
              # Boot wait exhausted: release the restart lock so a hub that
              # really died at boot is tried again.
              if ($restartingHub) {
                Write-Host '::warning::hub did not come back; a later restart will retry.'
                $restartingHub = $false; $fails = 0
              }
            }
            $cur = ''
            try { $cur = (Get-Content "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Raw -ErrorAction Stop).Trim() } catch { }
            $edgeOk = $false
            if ((Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and $cur) {
              try {
                $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-watch-probe.html"
                $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 10 "$cur/"
                $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
                if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeOk = $true }
              } catch { }
            }
            if ($edgeOk) { continue }
            Write-Host '::warning::tunnel dead; reopening.'
            Get-Process -Name cloudflared -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            $log = "$env:TEMP\cf2.log"
            cmd /c start "" /b "$cf" tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8090 --no-autoupdate --loglevel info `
              "1>$log" "2>$env:TEMP\cf2.err"
            $url = $null
            foreach ($k in 1..40) {
              Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
              $text = (Get-Content $log, "$env:TEMP\cf2.err" -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -join "`n"
              if ($text -match 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.trycloudflare\.com') { $url = $Matches[0]; break }
            }
            if (-not $url) { continue }
            $edgeReady = $false
            $probe = "$env:TEMP\hub-tunnel-probe2.html"
            foreach ($k in 1..30) {
              $code = curl.exe -sS -L -o $probe -w '%{http_code}' -m 15 "$url/"
              $body = Get-Content $probe -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
              if ($code -match '^[234]' -and $body -notmatch '(?i)1033') { $edgeReady = $true; break }
              Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
            }
            if (-not $edgeReady) { continue }
            $url | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-url.txt" -Encoding utf8 -NoNewline
            Write-Host "back up on $url"
            $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
            bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
              'slot=hub-windows' 'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
              "url=$url" "hubUrl=$url" "desktop=$url/d" "mobile=$url/m" `
              'auth=без пароля' 'label=${{ inputs.label }}'
          }

      - name: Final durable repository backup
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/backup-work.sh" --once \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/work-backup.log"

      - name: Snapshot audit/code on exit
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" SNAPSHOT_EXPORT_ALL_CHATS=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/snapshot-audit-code.sh" --once hub "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork" \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/snapshot-hub.log"

      - name: Clear the published session
        if: always()
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" 'slot=hub-windows' 'state=ended'

      - name: Save the models snapshot
        if: always()
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          try {
            $d = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/models/full' -TimeoutSec 20 -Headers @{'x-hub-token'='${{ inputs.token }}'}
            $ms = @($d.models)
            $free = @($ms | Where-Object { $_.free })
            $obj = [ordered]@{
              kind = 'NPM-Hub'
              hubCount = $ms.Count
              hubFree = $free.Count
              hubTop = @($free | Select-Object -First 8 | ForEach-Object { $_.fullId })
              hubSelected = $d.selected
            }
            ($obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4) | Out-File -FilePath "$env:TEMP\hub-models.json" -Encoding utf8
          } catch { }
          $env:GH_TOKEN = '${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}'
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" `
            'slot=hub-windows' 'file=models-hub-windows.json' `
            'kind=NPM-Hub' 'os=windows' `
            "json=$env:TEMP\hub-models.json"

      - name: Export OpenCode chats for all repositories
        # Runs even on a cancelled/expired job so the NEXT windows run can
        # restore every repo's sessions (chats/<name>.json -> session-state).
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CHAT_ALL_ROOT="$HOME" PUBLISH=1 \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/export-chats.sh" --all \
            2>&1 | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/export-chats.log"

      - name: Record the run in the history
        if: always()
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          # history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - see the Linux step.
          $env:GH_TOKEN = "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
          bash "$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 `
            "slot=hub-windows" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=windows" `
            "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$([DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ'))" `
            "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" `
            "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"

  # ── Linux Desktop VNC (parallel runner) ────────────────────────────────
  # A second, independent job next to `hub`. It stands up a headless Linux
  # desktop (openbox + xterm, Mesa software rendering) and exposes it through
  # x11vnc + noVNC + a cloudflared tunnel from the very start of the run, so
  # the hub gets a working graphical shell (an "Open the Linux screen" button)
  # without ever pressing Start. Kept alive by the same watchdog pattern as
  # the hub: dead desktop/tunnel gets restarted in-place.
  vnc:
    if: inputs.os == 'linux'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
    timeout-minutes: 360

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      - name: Install the desktop + VNC stack
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq \
            xvfb openbox xterm tint2 idesk x11vnc websockify novnc dbus-x11 \
            mesa-utils libgl1-mesa-dri libgl1 libegl1 libgles2 \
            libglu1-mesa libgbm1 x11-utils x11-xserver-utils \
            pcmanfm pulseaudio pavucontrol

      - name: Start the Linux desktop and open the tunnel
        run: |
          export VNC_PORT=5901 NOVNC_PORT=6081
          bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/start_desktop.sh" || {
            echo "::error::the Linux desktop VNC did not start."
            tail -30 $HUB_LOGS/xvfb.log $HUB_LOGS/openbox.log $HUB_LOGS/x11vnc.log 2>/dev/null
            exit 1
          }

          URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 6081 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel.log)
          if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
            echo "::error::no tunnel for the VNC desktop."
            tail -25 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/vnc-url

          # Pre-warm: the noVNC page must answer over the tunnel edge before
          # we hand the address to the panel.
          for i in $(seq 1 20); do
            code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -m 10 "$URL/vnc.html" || true)
            case "$code" in 2*|3*|4*) break ;; esac
            sleep 3
          done

          {
            echo "## Linux Desktop (VNC)"
            echo ""
            echo "**[Open the Linux screen]($URL/vnc.html)** - openbox + xterm + Mesa."
            echo ""
            echo "| | |"
            echo "|---|---|"
            echo "| noVNC | \`$URL/vnc.html\` |"
            echo "| VNC | \`127.0.0.1:5901\` (on the runner) |"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          echo "=================================================="
          echo " Linux Desktop VNC: $URL/vnc.html"
          echo "=================================================="

          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
              "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
              "url=$URL/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$URL/vnc.html" \
              $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2")") \
              "label=${{ inputs.label }}"

          # Z11 dual tunnel on the desktop VM as well.
          nohup env GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_keeper.sh" vnc >> "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.log" 2>&1 &
          echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/tunnel-keeper.pid"
          echo "tunnel keeper: vnc endpoint now carries main + reserve addresses"

          # Same lifelines as the hub job (Z10): this VM holds the desktop the
          # user actually watches - when the hub VM wedges, the queue + tmate
          # here stay reachable. Beacons land in control/rescue-vnc.json and
          # control/heartbeat-vnc.json, commands pick target=vnc.
          if [ "${{ inputs.rescue_ssh }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=vnc \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/rescue_ssh.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/rescue-ssh.pid"
            echo "rescue ssh daemon (vnc vm): -> control/rescue-vnc.json"
          fi
          if [ "${{ inputs.command_queue }}" = "true" ]; then
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" GITHUB_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" CONTROL_TARGET=vnc \
              HUB_LABEL='${{ inputs.label }}' \
              nohup bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/hub_control.sh" >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.log" 2>&1 &
            echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control.pid"
            echo "control daemon (vnc vm): queue + heartbeat; reopen-tunnel reopens the VNC tunnel"
          fi

      - name: Keep the VNC session alive
        run: |
          PIDFILE="$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-6081.pid"
          cleanup_vnc() {
            local code="${1:-143}"
            trap - TERM INT
            if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then
              local pid; pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
              [ -z "$pid" ] || kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            pkill -f "websockify.*6081" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:6081" 2>/dev/null || true
            # Background lifelines started above: same "Complete job" hang rule.
            pkill -f "[h]ub_control.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[r]escue_ssh.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[t]unnel_keeper.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
            rm -f "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-6081-reserve.pid" 2>/dev/null || true
            tmate -S "$HUB_LOGS/tmate.sock" kill-session >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            # The X stack is started detached by start_desktop.sh and the
            # runner waits for it too - leaving Xvfb/openbox/x11vnc running
            # hangs "Complete job" exactly like the hub's daemons did.
            pkill -f "Xvfb ${VNC_DISPLAY:-:99}" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "[o]penbox" 2>/dev/null || true
            pkill -f "x11vnc.*${VNC_DISPLAY:-:99}" 2>/dev/null || true
            # Same as the hub job: `if: always()` does not survive a cancel.
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=vnc" "state=ended" \
              >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            exit "$code"
          }
          trap 'cleanup_vnc 143' TERM INT
          VFAILS=0
          VRESTARTING=0
          for i in $(seq 1 1400); do
            sleep 15
            # Same rule as the hub watchdog: a busy CPU (a game or a build in
            # the desktop) can make one probe bleed over its timeout. Restart
            # the desktop only after several consecutive misses, and only if a
            # restart is not already in progress.
            if curl -sf -o /dev/null -m 20 "http://127.0.0.1:6081/vnc.html"; then
              VFAILS=0
            else
              VFAILS=$((VFAILS + 1))
              echo "::warning::VNC probe missed ($VFAILS consecutive)."
            fi
            if [ "$VFAILS" -ge 3 ] && [ "$VRESTARTING" = "0" ]; then
              echo "::warning::desktop VNC stopped answering; restarting it."
              VRESTARTING=1
              pkill -f "websockify.*6081" 2>/dev/null || true
              export VNC_PORT=5901 NOVNC_PORT=6081
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/start_desktop.sh" || true
              for boot in $(seq 1 12); do
                if curl -sf -o /dev/null -m 20 "http://127.0.0.1:6081/vnc.html"; then
                  VFAILS=0; VRESTARTING=0
                  echo "::warning::VNC is back."
                  break
                fi
                sleep 5
              done
              if [ "$VRESTARTING" = "1" ]; then
                echo "::warning::VNC did not come back; a later restart will retry."
                VRESTARTING=0; VFAILS=0
              fi
            fi
            CUR=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url" 2>/dev/null || echo)
            PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || echo)
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$CUR" ] \
              && bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/tunnel_health.sh" "$CUR" "/vnc.html"; then
              continue
            fi
            # Same stale-cloudflared cleanup as the hub job above; bracket
            # pattern so pkill never matches this shell's own command line.
            if [ -n "$PID" ] && kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
            pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:6081" 2>/dev/null || true
            sleep 1
            echo "::warning::VNC tunnel dead; reopening."
            URL=$(bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/open_tunnel.sh" 6081 $HUB_LOGS/vnc-tunnel2.log) || continue
            [ -n "$URL" ] || continue
            echo "$URL" > $HUB_LOGS/vnc-url
            echo "VNC back up on $URL/vnc.html"
            GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
              bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" \
                "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
                "url=$URL/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$URL/vnc.html" \
                $([ -s "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" ] && echo "url2=$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2")") \
                "label=${{ inputs.label }}"
          done
          cleanup_vnc 0

      - name: Clear the published VNC session
        if: always()
        run: |
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" "slot=vnc" "state=ended"

      - name: Record the run in the history
        if: always()
        run: |
          # One small file per run, filed under the day and the weekday it
          # belongs to: history/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<Wd>/run-<runNumber>.json - the
          # diary the panel groups by day, and unlike the Actions UI it does not
          # disappear when GitHub prunes old runs.
          STARTED=""
          if [ -f "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" ]; then
            STARTED="$(date -u -d "@$(( $(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) / 1000 ))" '+%Y-%m-%d' 2>/dev/null || true)"
          fi
          GH_TOKEN="${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" \
            bash "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/tools/publish_session.sh" journal=1 \
              "slot=vnc" "kind=VNC" "os=linux" \
              "conclusion=${{ job.status }}" "endedAt=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" \
              ${STARTED:+journal_date="$STARTED"} \
              "handoff=${{ inputs.handoff }}" \
              "runUrl=https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" \
              2>&1 | tail -5 || echo "::warning::run history record failed"

parts.text:
Now I have a very clear picture. This is the "npm-hub" / Zen Hub system. It's a GitHub Actions workflow (`hub.yml`) that can be triggered in any repo that carries it. It runs a web hub on a GitHub-hosted runner (or self-hosted, based on `inputs.runner_linux` / `runner_windows` labels). The hub clones the user's repos into `~/hub-work` (restore-work.sh), so you can work on any repo from one session.

The user asks: "например я хочу подключиться к npm hub ранеру что у меня в каком то моем репо" -> "ну например хочу подключиться к его ранеру zen-panel" -> "нет я имел ввиду свободное переключение между репо и их ранерами".

So the user wants free switching between repos and their runners. In this system:

- The workflow `hub.yml` is a `workflow_dispatch` with inputs including `runner_linux`, `runner_windows`, `label`, `os`, `handoff`, `rescue_ssh`, `command_queue`, etc.
- The runner is chosen by `runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}` and `runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_windows }}` — that means the user can type the runner label at trigger time! So they CAN freely choose the runner.
- The hub itself clones multiple repos into `hub-work`, so you can switch between repos within one session.

Let me look at the workflow's `on: workflow_dispatch` inputs at the top of hub.yml to confirm the runner selection. The output was truncated at the start. Let me read the head of hub.yml.

state.output:
name: NPM Hub

# The third agent: npm-hub on a runner, in a browser tab of the panel.
#
# WHAT IT IS
#   npm-hub/ is a tools dashboard with xterm terminal tabs: it detects the
#   installed AI CLI agents (claude, gemini, codex, copilot, opencode and
#   friends) and opens each in its own terminal session, with a file manager
#   and a live model registry on top. All of that logic already lives in the
#   repo - this workflow optionally preinstalls the CLIs, starts the server and
#   publishes the address, the same way the desks and the other agents do.
#
#   No work branch, no autosave: the hub edits nothing by itself, it is a
#   launcher. What outlives the runner is the models snapshot
#   (models-hub-<os>.json, one per OS) and whatever the user saves through the panel.
#
# AUTH
#   Panel-launched runs carry a gate token (the `token` input, generated per
#   launch): without ?zt= the hub answers 401 on every page, API call and
#   terminal socket. The tunnel address itself stays unguessable and dies
#   with the run (six hours at most).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      os:
        description: "Runner OS"
        type: choice
        options: [linux, windows]
        default: linux
      label:
        description: "Name for this session"
        type: string
        default: "hub"
      token:
        description: "Hub gate token, generated by the panel (empty = no gate)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      gh_token:
        description: "GitHub PAT for the server-side /gh proxy (empty = proxy off)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      runner_linux:
        description: "Runner for the Linux job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "ubuntu-latest"
      runner_windows:
        description: "Runner for the Windows job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "windows-latest"
      preinstall:
        description: "Install all CLI agents at startup (minutes); off = each installs at first click"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      replace:
        description: "Replace an active session run"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff:
        description: "This run takes over a session that another runner handed over"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff_from:
        description: "runId of the runner that handed the session over"
        type: string
        default: ""
      rescue_ssh:
        description: "tmate rescue shell published to session-state control/rescue.json (lifeline when the hub+web die)"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      command_queue:
        description: "safe command queue on session-state control/queue.json (whitelisted ops only)"
        type: boolean
        default: true

concurrency:
  group: zen-panel-session-${{ github.repository }}
  # A handoff run must NOT cancel the runner it takes over from: that runner
  # saves, waits until this one has published itself, and only then steps aside.
  # A manual «заменить» from the panel still cancels the old run.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ inputs.replace && !inputs.handoff }}

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  HUB_LOGS: /home/runner/.npm-hub/logs

metadata.output:
name: NPM Hub

# The third agent: npm-hub on a runner, in a browser tab of the panel.
#
# WHAT IT IS
#   npm-hub/ is a tools dashboard with xterm terminal tabs: it detects the
#   installed AI CLI agents (claude, gemini, codex, copilot, opencode and
#   friends) and opens each in its own terminal session, with a file manager
#   and a live model registry on top. All of that logic already lives in the
#   repo - this workflow optionally preinstalls the CLIs, starts the server and
#   publishes the address, the same way the desks and the other agents do.
#
#   No work branch, no autosave: the hub edits nothing by itself, it is a
#   launcher. What outlives the runner is the models snapshot
#   (models-hub-<os>.json, one per OS) and whatever the user saves through the panel.
#
# AUTH
#   Panel-launched runs carry a gate token (the `token` input, generated per
#   launch): without ?zt= the hub answers 401 on every page, API call and
#   terminal socket. The tunnel address itself stays unguessable and dies
#   with the run (six hours at most).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      os:
        description: "Runner OS"
        type: choice
        options: [linux, windows]
        default: linux
      label:
        description: "Name for this session"
        type: string
        default: "hub"
      token:
        description: "Hub gate token, generated by the panel (empty = no gate)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      gh_token:
        description: "GitHub PAT for the server-side /gh proxy (empty = proxy off)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      runner_linux:
        description: "Runner for the Linux job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "ubuntu-latest"
      runner_windows:
        description: "Runner for the Windows job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "windows-latest"
      preinstall:
        description: "Install all CLI agents at startup (minutes); off = each installs at first click"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      replace:
        description: "Replace an active session run"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff:
        description: "This run takes over a session that another runner handed over"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff_from:
        description: "runId of the runner that handed the session over"
        type: string
        default: ""
      rescue_ssh:
        description: "tmate rescue shell published to session-state control/rescue.json (lifeline when the hub+web die)"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      command_queue:
        description: "safe command queue on session-state control/queue.json (whitelisted ops only)"
        type: boolean
        default: true

concurrency:
  group: zen-panel-session-${{ github.repository }}
  # A handoff run must NOT cancel the runner it takes over from: that runner
  # saves, waits until this one has published itself, and only then steps aside.
  # A manual «заменить» from the panel still cancels the old run.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ inputs.replace && !inputs.handoff }}

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  HUB_LOGS: /home/runner/.npm-hub/logs

jobs:

Да, в этой системе (Zen Hub) свободное переключение уже заложено — но по двум осям, и важно не путать:

**Репозитории — свободно.** Хаб держит все твои репо в `~/hub-work/*` (их восстанавливает `tools/restore-work.sh`), а вкладка Files/терминал работает с любым из них. Сейчас, например, запущен workflow `zen-panel`, а PWD — `NimbusSeat-Runner/code`.

**Раннер — свободно на этапе запуска.** В `hub.yml` раннер это входной параметр, а не хардкод:
- `runner_linux` (default `ubuntu-latest`)
- `runner_windows` (default `windows-latest`)
```yaml
runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}    # hub.yml:79
```
То есть в диалоге запуска панели (или через `gh workflow run hub.yml -f runner_linux=... `) можно вписать любой лейбл, включая `self-hosted` — см. `pc-local/runner/README.md`.

**Где «свободы» нет (ограничение GitHub, не кода):** self-hosted раннер, зарегистрированный в репо A, не виден workflow репо B. `self-hosted` в репо B подхватит только раннеры, зарегистрированные в B (или в организации). GitHub-hosted лейблы (`ubuntu-latest`, `windows-latest`) работают в любом репо.

Хочешь «один self-hosted на все репо» — регистрируй на уровне **organization**: тогда `runner_linux: self-hosted` сработает из любого репо орг. Хочешь — покажу, как это поправить в `pc-local/runner/setup.sh`.
